Mortgage rates moved higher this week, ending a four-week streak of declines, as bond investors grew more nervous about inflation.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rate was 7.28% this week through Wednesday, according to Freddie Mac data, up from 7.11% a week earlier.
Mortgage News Daily, which uses different data to calculate rates, put the average mortgage rate at 7.46% as of Wednesday, up from 7.18% at the beginning of last week.
The jump came after the 10-year Treasury yield, which mortgage rates closely track, moved higher last week after inflation data for consumer and producer prices came in hotter than expected, cementing odds that the Federal Reserve will hike benchmark interest rates at its December meeting.
The Fed doesn't directly control mortgage rates, but expectations about the central bank's future actions influence their direction.
"The debate has shifted from whether the Fed hikes in December to how aggressively it moves ," Realtor.com senior economist Anthony Smith said in a statement. "That is a tough backdrop for mortgage rates heading into what is already a seasonally slow stretch for the housing market."
Here are the current purchase mortgage rates for today, Thursday, November 19, 2026 , according to the latest Zillow data:
Here are the current refinance mortgage rates for today, Thursday, November 19, 2026 , according to the latest Zillow data:
Use Yahoo Finance's mortgage calculator below to see how various mortgage rates will impact your monthly payments and overall loan costs.
Bookmark the Yahoo Finance mortgage payment calculator and keep it handy as you shop for homes and lenders. Be sure to use the dropdown to include private mortgage insurance costs and HOA dues if they apply to you. These monthly expenses, along with your mortgage principal and interest rate, will give you a realistic idea of your monthly payment.
Two categories determine mortgage rates : those you can control and those you cannot.
What factors can you control? First, you can compare the mortgage lenders to find the one that gives you the lowest rate and fees.
Second, lenders typically extend lower rates to people with higher credit scores, lower debt-to-income (DTI) ratios , and considerable down payments. If you can save more or pay down debt before securing a mortgage, a lender will probably give you a better interest rate.
What factors can you not control? In short, the economy.
The list of ways the economy impacts mortgage rates is long, but here are the basic details. If the economy — for example, employment rates — is struggling, mortgage rates decrease to encourage borrowing, which helps boost the economy. If the economy is strong, mortgage rates go up to temper spending.
With all other factors being equal, mortgage refinance rates are typically slightly higher than purchase rates. So don't be surprised if your refinance rate is higher than you may have expected.
Two of the most common mortgage terms are 30-year and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages . Both lock in your rate for the entire loan term.
A 30-year mortgage is popular because it has relatively low monthly payments. But it comes with a higher interest rate than shorter terms, and because you're accumulating interest for three decades, you'll pay a lot of interest in the long run.
A 15-year mortgage can be a good choice because it has a lower rate than longer terms, so you'll pay less interest over time. You'll also pay off your mortgage much faster. But your monthly payments will be higher because you're paying off the same loan amount in half the time.
Basically, 30-year mortgages are more affordable from month to month, while 15-year mortgages are cheaper in the long run.
According to Yahoo Finance's weekly survey of lenders with the lowest rates , some of the banks with the lowest median mortgage rates are Chase and Citibank . However, it's a good idea to shop around for the best rate, not just with banks, but also with credit unions and companies specializing in mortgage lending.
Yes, 2.75% is an amazing mortgage rate. You're unlikely to get a 2.75% rate in today's market unless you take on an assumable mortgage from a seller who locked in this rate in 2020 or 2021, when rates were at all-time lows.
According to Freddie Mac, the lowest-ever 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 2.65%. This was the national average in January 2021. It is extremely unlikely that rates will dip below 3% again anytime soon.
Some experts say it's worth refinancing when you can lock in a rate that's 2% less than your current mortgage rate. Others say 1% is the magic number. It all depends on your financial goals when refinancing, how long you plan to stay in the same house, and on your break-even point after paying the refinance closing costs.
The interest rates provided by the Zillow Lender Marketplace are national averages rounded to the nearest hundredth. The rates featured in today's daily rate article were provided to Yahoo Finance the previous day. The rates in this article are current as of November 18, 2026, at 2:59 p.m. ET.

DANIELA AMODEI: Thank you for having us.
DARIO AMODEI: Thank you for having us.
SORKIN: Here's where I want to start this. When I first met you, you basically just practically started the company. And I'm so curious — you understood scaling laws at the beginning, perhaps better than anybody, but did you ever expect three, four, five years later here we would be and be talking about evaluation that starts with a T?
DARIO AMODEI: You know, the funny thing is, you look at the scaling laws and they're a line on a piece of paper, right? They predict that a model will have certain cognitive capabilities that will be capable of certain economic tasks. But it's one thing to kind of draw that line, and it's a totally different thing to see the consequences out in the world. And so I would say the scaling laws kind of imply that the technology and hopefully our work within it would — would have this scale. But I don't think we really believed it until it actually happened.
SORKIN: And it's happening right now. Daniela, this is now going to be the largest public benefit corporation to go public. And I think when Dario and I and our other co-founders were starting the organization, you know, we learned about this concept of a public benefit corporation. It really spoke to us, because we said, well, that's exactly what we're trying to do. We're really trying to do something that we do think can have this incredible economic value and impact, but we want it to be baked into essentially our structure that we also have to balance that against building things that are good for people.
SORKIN: OK, so here's the question. How do you balance the idea of growth and the idea of, for example, pacing at this point? This is something you have talked a lot about, pacing, given some of the safety concerns around AI? And how should the investor class think about those competing interests?
DARIO AMODEI: So, this, you know, this is one of the central tensions at the heart of the company. But it's really, because this technology is so powerful, it has so many effects in the world, it's something that every company in this space will have to face, whether they want to or not. We're just facing it more explicitly and more thoughtfully. And so, you think about something like pacing, the idea behind pacing was, you know, imagine that you have — you're driving your car at 60 miles an hour, and then you discover or invent something that could let you drive the car at 200 miles an hour, right? This is models building themselves, recursive self-improvement. What we have done with pacing is essentially said, look, you know, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour, spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus, we spend building the model in the right way. And you know, I think, in the long run, that will work out pretty well for the investors as well, because the company that builds the safest, that has trust of the customers and the enterprises of the world, I think that is the company that's going to be both best for society and, in the long run, I hope, best for the performance of the company. DARIO AMODEI:  I think that's one of the very few topics we're not allowed to talk about.
DANIELA AMODEI:  I think, you know, I think maybe the way I would put it is, Anthropic has always been a very long-term-focused company, right? We have always been thinking about, how is this technology going to be beneficial to people in the future, but also what can it do for people today? And so while today is a super exciting milestone and we're obviously really, really excited about it, I think it's, for us, it's like one stop on the journey, right? articles.title_orig: AMD sheds nearly $100 billion in market value as China chip concerns hit AI stocks
articles.title_zh: AMD sheds nearly $100 billion in market value as China chip concerns hit AI stocks
articles.content_orig:
Concerns about balance sheets and valuations in the artificial intelligence sector have hit the market hard since October, and investors who have shorted publicly traded tech companies in the AI trade have profited. Most investors don't think as much about "shorting" debt, but there will be a way through exchange-traded funds to profit from widening credit default swap spreads of top AI companies.
Both Tuttle Capital and Defiance ETFs have filed for funds that target the credit default swaps of companies closely linked to the AI trade, from CoreWeave and Oracle to the Magnificent Seven: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Microsoft Corporation, Nvidia, Tesla, and Apple.
Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier. CDS is a closely watched indicator of issuer health in the debt markets, especially in the AI market this year. The ETFs are designed to gain when the CDS spreads of these companies widen, either as a group in the case of a Magnificent Seven CDS fund, or individually in the case of proposed ETFs targeting Oracle, CoreWeave and Meta. The funds would lose value when the market assesses the creditworthiness of these debt issuers as improving.
Both ETF managers filed for CoreWeave and Oracle CDS funds, specifically, among broader AI and semiconductor company CDS portfolios.
If the exchange-traded fund managers get approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission, these portfolios would be the first of their kind in an ETF market that has become more aggressive in recent years about launching higher-risk strategies revolving around more complex financial instruments than just public stocks and bonds. The ETF managers plan to employ leverage in the portfolios, which both increases risk and the potential for outsized returns on any given day, similar to the way existing single-stock leverage and inverse ETFs function.
The ETF managers say these CDS funds can serve an important role in a market on edge about AI debt.
"As AI infrastructure investment accelerates and companies take on significant capital commitments to fund that growth, we see an opportunity to give investors more targeted tools to manage credit risk and hedge potential financial stress across some of the biggest names driving the AI buildout," Sylvia Jablonski, CIO of Defiance ETFs, said in a statement to CNBC.
Neocloud companies like CoreWeave are a major focus for AI skeptics, an AI bubble watch compounded by the exit of Jensen Huang from Nvidia, who is seen as a critical player in financing the AI buildout, with Nvidia called by some the "central bank of AI ."
Apollo Global Management CEO Marc Rowan on Tuesday said that neocloud company AI projects could face an existential crisis if Nvidia funding dries up. "There was a strong incentive for Nvidia as a business matter to get these projects off the ground," Rowan said in an interview with CNBC's " Squawk on the Street ." "If that banking function, that guarantor function, gets taken away, access to capital for a large number of neoclouds is going to disappear."
In its earnings filings and conference call on Tuesday, Nvidia shifted the tone in discussing the way it finances the AI ecosystem.
Matthew Tuttle, founder and CEO of Tuttle Capital Management, said it is less likely that these ETFs will find an audience among retail investors than smaller institutional players.
"It may be a stretch for the average retail guy," he said, but he added that having managed leveraged and inverse ETFs, it is clear that many investors "get interested" when a particular asset is seeing outsized moves, as has been the case with AI company-linked CDS in 2026. "The stuff that moves a lot is the stuff that tends to generate the most interest," he said.
Both prospectuses stress that these funds are not designed to move inversely to the reference companies' stocks and can lose money while a company's shares decline. They also note these funds don't short bonds or bet directly against a company's stock, and to buy CDS protection, they pay premiums, which are a unique cost to the fund manager whether or not credit conditions worsen.
The CDS of these companies have been on the move in a major way as part of the AI trade over the past year.
CoreWeave's 9.75% bond due in 2031 is yielding close to 16%, while spreads on its five-year credit default swaps were recently between 1,100-1,200. Spreads over 1,000 are generally considered a sign of distress.
CoreWeave executives have taken their messaging about the debt public, with co-founder and chief strategy officer Brian Venturo posting on X.com on Wednesday that he had purchased $30 million in unsecured company bonds and was going to hold them until maturity in 2031. "I've never been more confident in CoreWeave," he wrote.
Oracle CDS contracts have moved up over the past year from below 80 to a current range above 300.
The CDS spreads on the biggest tech companies, including Amazon and Meta as examples, rose over 100% within the past year, as their free cash flow turned negative from spending heavily on AI. Even though the market is much less concerned about their balance sheets than that of the neoclouds, major tech company CDS spreads did hit five-year highs earlier this month.
Tuttle said that these ETFs, if approved, would be the "easiest" to use for smaller institutions and family offices that want CDS exposure and "are either too small to trade with the Goldmans of the world or lack the in-house expertise to trade CDS on their own."
"It is a different way to hedge the AI trade," Tuttle said.
ETF investing experts expressed skepticism about this approach and market reception. "I don't see much demand materializing for these types of products," said Nate Geraci, president of NovaDius Wealth Management. But he added it does make sense to target these ETFs "at retail investors who are seeing scary headlines around AI capex spending. Yet another way to speculate (gamble)," he said.
Todd Sohn, chief ETF strategist at Baird Strategas, said he foresees confusion with how these funds will work. "How many non-professionals know what CDS are?" he said.
Tuttle says it won't take billions in assets to make an ETF focused on AI CDS a minor financial success. "My criteria is I want to see a runway to $20 million, which is about our breakeven. I see it here. It doesn't mean it will happen, but I think we have a decent chance."
— CNBC's Michelle Fox contributed to this report

articles.title_orig: China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars
articles.title_zh: China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars
articles.content_orig:
Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’
China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.
The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it said was the protection of diplomatic immunity.
The statement affirmed that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought”, but stopped short of suggesting the beginnings of a framework for denuclearisation.
The meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump has dominated the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit this week, with China, the host, promising it would be “groundbreaking”.
“We are really making history,” Trump told Xi and Putin at the start of the meeting. “No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement.”
Putin told a press conference later that the three men had had a “free discussion” and now had a “mutual understanding”.
Some had hopes that the talks, which lasted about one hour and 20 minutes, could be used to discuss reductions in arms between the world’s three largest nuclear powers. Beijing has previously rebuffed Trump’s advances to join such talks, pointing to the larger US and Russian stockpiles. On Thursday, though, Xi called for nuclear weapons to “be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of [them]”.
The language of the declaration around nuclear war is the same as that previously issued by the five permanent members of the UN security council, which includes France and the UK.
“The real test will be whether the three countries follow through on their stated commitment to discuss nuclear risk reduction and preventing nuclear proliferation,” said Patricia Kim, an expert on Chinese foreign policy at the Brookings Institution, a US thinktank. Even the suggestion that China would engage was significant, said Yun Sun, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center.
Analysts had said that the meeting’s primary significance was in its optics. “Overall, very little of substance seems to have been accomplished … This summit appears to have been all about the symbolism and prestige value,” said Prof William Hurst, from the University of Cambridge’s Centre for Geopolitics. Putin pushed back at the suggestion the summit had just been a photo-op. “It is a serious collaborative work,” he said.
In the declaration, the men “committed themselves to maintaining strategic stability and international security”.
First among their concerns was “promoting UN reform so that it may respond more effectively to global challenges”. Sun said this was a favourite topic of China’s and showed that Beijing was “flexing its diplomatic muscles”. She said: “It is able to set the agenda and the deliverables according to its priorities … and make other great powers accept them.”
The declaration also agreed that “the international criminal court [ICC] and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction”. Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant and so the clause added to the perception that he has done well from the summit. Since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, the Russian president has been treated as an international pariah by Kyiv’s allies and he has not been to an Apec summit in years.
Hurst said: “This was no Yalta moment, but it was certainly a solid public demonstration of Russia’s (and Putin’s) continuing relevance and power. It’s yet another example of Putin playing a poor hand to maximum effect.”
Xi, his status as a global powerbroker now assured, began the morning by addressing Apec leaders, reiterating the themes of trade openness and innovation he has emphasised throughout the summit. He made an appeal for regional harmony, saying: “Members of Apec are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other.”
However, Apec affairs appeared to take a back seat for most of the day, with business dominating the discussions. For all the camaraderie on display, relations are complex. Russia is under US sanctions over the Ukraine war, while China and the US spent much of the last year engaged in an escalating tit-for-tat trade war before Trump and Xi called a truce .
Trump and Putin earlier held a separate meeting – their first since August 2025 – with the US president calling the Russian his “friend”. The peace declaration said the three countries planned “to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations”. That was important, said Shan Guo from Hutong Research, a Shanghai-based advisory firm, but “now let’s see if the US will lift sanctions”.
Trump and Xi then held their third bilateral of this year. Xi said the US-China relationship was “generally stable and positive”, according to state media. But he cautioned Washington over Taiwan, saying the US “must keep doing the right thing to avoid major setbacks in US-China relations”.
Another watched-for topic lacking detailed findings was that of AI. Xi said the two countries should “enhance communication and coordination to guard against security risks … and ensure that AI remains under human control at all times”.
Ultimately, the lack of breakthroughs might suit China, which has no appetite to move beyond the role of convener, said Kim. “Beijing has little interest in taking on the diplomatic risks of brokering an actual peace agreement in Ukraine or resolving the conflict with Iran. That would entangle China in conflicts it would rather avoid,” she said.

articles.title_orig: 'Come to Moscow,' Putin urges Europeans after Shenzhen summit
articles.title_zh: 'Come to Moscow,' Putin urges Europeans after Shenzhen summit
articles.content_orig:
President Vladimir Putin said Thursday that Russia will not negotiate with Ukraine on a limited ceasefire, citing a Ukrainian strike this week on a major bridge connecting Russia and Ukraine's Russian-occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Putin made the remarks to reporters in Russian after meeting with President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China. He said he had discussed the possibility of a ceasefire in certain areas of Ukraine, but would not move forward with negotiations after Ukraine's strike on the Kerch Bridge, according to the Russian state news agencies.
The 12-mile bridge, which Putin ceremonially opened himself in 2018, is hugely symbolic as it links the Russian mainland with Crimea — territory that Russian forces occupied about four years earlier. The missile strike this week wasn't the first time Ukraine had targeted the piece of infrastructure, but it inflicted severe damage. Russia also struck two major bridges in Kyiv the same day.
Putin played down the bridge's strategic importance on Thursday and said he had heard the calls "from all sides" for a naval ceasefire or a suspension of strikes on energy facilities, but he ruled out direct negotiations with Ukraine, citing the attack on the bridge.
"Honestly, I discussed the issue with my colleagues at the Security Council, and I asked them to think about it and go back to the issue, so that we could reach some agreements," Putin said, according to Russian state news agency TASS. "However, we will not make agreements after strikes on the Crimean Bridge. We will respond to these strikes."
Putin vowed that Russia's retaliation for the strike on the bridge would be severe, TASS reported.
While Putin claims frequently to want peace, he denies that Russia started the war with his order for a full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, and Russia's attacks on Ukraine have been relentless.
It's not clear how much Ukraine came up in Mr. Trump's one-on-one meeting with Putin on Wednesday, or in the meeting with both Putin and Xi on Thursday. Last week, the White House said Ukraine wouldn't be a topic of discussion, but before he left for Asia, Mr. Trump said the three leaders would be discussing the war. The White House readout of the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting was sparse on detail, and did not mention Ukraine.
Meanwhile, Mr. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff have been in Germany to meet with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and other European leaders about Ukraine and other topics.
Kushner said they discussed the "latest efforts to achieve a just, lasting and durable peace in Ukraine."
"We are grateful for his leadership, constructive engagement, and close partnership as we work together toward our shared goal of ending this terrible war and building a secure and prosperous future for Ukraine and Europe," Kushner posted to X .
Merz, speaking to reporters after the meeting, called the China summit a photo-op and said the trilateral format "will not bring peace" in Ukraine.
As he went to shake Putin's hand before an earlier meeting Wednesday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China, Mr. Trump referred to the Russian leader as "my friend."
"Who is he?" the president said, pointing at Putin and smiling. "He's my friend."

articles.title_orig: ‘GTA VI’ Beats ‘The Odyssey’ Revenue On Release Day, Estimate Says
articles.title_zh: ‘GTA VI’ Beats ‘The Odyssey’ Revenue On Release Day, Estimate Says
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto VI is here at last and gamers around the world can finally play after it launched at midnight globally. So far the game, which takes up a whopping 212GB on your PlayStation5 or Xbox , is receiving rave reviews . GTA 6 is streaming all over Twitch and the memes, clips and hot takes are pouring in.
Digital marketing firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 pre-orders have already topped $1.65 billion in sales. GTA 6 costs $79.99 for PS5 and Xbox , with an "ultimate" version priced at $99.99.
Players began pre-loading GTA 6 last week, even though they probably had to clear some space on their consoles. Millions of people are expected to take time off work and school to play GTA 6 . Xbox has a doctor's note from DJ Khaled (aka Dr. Xbox) that may be the excuse you need (but you'll probably want to clear it with your boss either way).
PlayStation's network suffered a brief outage Wednesday afternoon as the game became available and players made the required update to their consoles. But since Wednesday evening, it's been smooth sailing.
Here's what people are saying about GTA VI today:
GTA 6 received quite a bit of attention ahead of its release after Rockstar revealed some of the celebrities it tapped to be radio hosts for the in-game stations, including big names like Lana Del Rey and Bad Bunny. Now that the game is out, we're discovering even more celebrities and musicians that were kept a secret. Here's a look at some of the others that have been confirmed so far:
Charlamagne tha God and Ivy Rivera on Early AF Radio
Antonio Carbonaro and Seth Troxler on Circoloco Records
PinkPantheress and the Dare on Stockyard FM
Earlier today, we also learned that parody legend "Weird" Al Yankovic hosts the game's '80s hits station, Vice City FM.
We're sure more celebrity cameos will be found as people dig deeper into the game, but it's been a pretty stacked cast so far.
With 13 years between GTA 5 and GTA 6 , Rockstar had a lot of time to polish the game world and pack it with plenty of detail that has left both reviewers and players stunned . But all that detail takes a toll when the action gets going. The game targets 30 frames per second (FPS) for normal gameplay, but some players have reported it dropping to 15 to 20 FPS during fights on the base PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S consoles.
If you're not a gamer, FPS essentially determines how "smooth" a game feels and describes how many individual frames of gameplay are shown every second. Many gamers view 30 FPS as the floor for smooth gameplay, and 60 FPS or higher as the gold standard. Once you start dropping below 30, gameplay can feel choppy and laggy.
The top-end Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5 Pro appear to have an easier time sticking close to that 30 FPS mark due to their more powerful hardware. If you're interested in a technical breakdown, you can check out Digital Foundry's excellent GTA 6 tech review .
One beloved GTA 6 meme may be heading off into retirement with the new game's launch, but it has already birthed a hilarious new one. X user @MurdoinkGS added a green screen to the in-game phone screen in a clip of a player mindlessly running over beachgoers in a vehicle. The internet understood the assignment, replacing the green screen effect with all kinds of distracting content, ranging from a Hasan Piker Twitch stream to Pokémon Go and more.
It hasn't totally broken the internet so far, but the launch of GTA 6 helped set a new internet usage record , according to Frankfurt, Germany-based internet exchange operator DE-CIX.
Wednesday night, data throughput across DE-CIX's internet exchanges worldwide reached a new high of 33.03 TB per second. Data transfer and usage during the midnight launch of GTA 6 was 25% higher than usual, the company said.
Data traffic also spiked about 20% after the GTA 6 download period opened on Nov. 10, DE-CIX said, with roughly 13 downloads of the game every second in Germany.
If you're getting up to some nefarious stuff in GTA 6 , you might want to watch your back. Players have found Dexter Morgan's apartment and boat from the Showtime series Dexter in the game. We haven't seen any signs that the Florida-based serial killer himself is in the game, but you can find his "toolkit" on the roof of his apartment building — complete with a syringe for incapacitating his targets.
One of the GTA series' biggest strengths is its penchant for pop-culture satire and references, so it isn't surprising to see there's a Dexter reference in Leonida — a fictional Florida. We're sure players will be discovering pop-culture references throughout the game for a long, long time to come.
When the release date for Grand Theft Auto VI was announced earlier this year, U.S. Army soldiers at Fort Stewart, Georgia, were given the opportunity to sign up for a four-day weekend off to play the game — if they re-enlisted for two years of additional military service.
According to Task & Purpose , a website focused on the U.S. military community, 43 soldiers in the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion took the offer.
An Army spokesperson told the site that most participants "already had reasons to remain in the military" and described the gaming offer as "an added bonus rather than necessarily the deciding factor."
A Singaporean couple who drew up an agreement with "rules" for playing GTA 6 once it launched said it was meant as a joke. But Julian Tay and Lisa Chan told CNN that a lot of the online reaction showed people may have missed the point (which is not exactly a first on the internet).
The agreement, which runs from launch day, Nov. 19, through Nov. 29 allows Tay to play as much as he wants over that time, with questions and requests on hold until an in-game mission ends. Any hugs or errands have to wait for a break in between missions, and dismissive comments from Chan if Tay fails a mission aren't allowed. It also stipulates that everything that happens in game is fictional.
When they posted a video of the contract last month, the couple heard some immediate feedback from many online who thought the contract raised red flags.
"There was quite a lot of backlash when we made the video, and everyone was like, 'Oh, leave him,'" Tay told CNN .
But Chan said it was always intended to be tongue-in-cheek, theorizing people were maybe projecting some insecurities about their own relationships onto them. She told CNN she plans to watch him play the game, and even put together a GTA-themed care package for him.
One of the biggest benefits of taking 13 years to release a game? Rockstar had plenty of time to make the map absolutely massive. Now, the map has been fully revealed, showing just how large Leonida is. One streamer, who goes by AngelMelly online, said she spent eight hours fully revealing the map in-game.
Considering the amount of detail on the map, ranging from the bustling Vice City to swamplands and beaches, it looks like GTA 6 players will have enough to sink their teeth into for a long time.
If you were ever doubting the cultural reach of a video game launch, even singer-songwriter Tinashe is getting in on the GTA 6 festivities. The Grammy-nominated artist streamed herself playing the new title last night, leading to some hilarious clips, including one of her crashing a plane.
She's definitely not alone, either: Twitch, the most popular platform for live-streaming games, showed that GTA 6 peaked at more than 3 million live viewers across tens of thousands of channels.
About to jump into GTA 6 for the first time? It's worth your time to bone up on some spoiler-free, early-game tips. Thankfully, fans who have already spent hours in-game have been sharing some essential tips to help you get off on the right foot, whether it's easy ways to earn money or how to ditch the cops with an outfit change.

Chinese technology firms are bracing for impacts on their ambitious artificial intelligence plans as the U.S. tightens restrictions on China 's access to the world's cutting-edge chips.
Chinese tech giant Alibaba , which on Thursday announced another quarter of strong revenue growth for its global AI cloud and compute services, warned that the new U.S. rules could affect some of its global data center expansion plans. It said it was still assessing the repercussions.
The Trump administration this week issued new rules in the wake of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, following the news that he’d had an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
The rules now restrict remote computing access through data centers in third countries, the latest U.S. move to curtail China’s abilities to use advanced Nvidia chips to train its increasingly capable AI models.
Alibaba's AI revenues are surging as demand grows
As the technology race between the two superpowers intensifies, existing U.S. export restrictions already barred China from getting the world’s most powerful chips.
But some Chinese companies have been able to bypass those restrictions by renting remote computing access to train AI models, pushing the U.S. to close what some policymakers called a loophole.
As global AI usage grows, Alibaba has been expanding its capabilities across chips, cloud infrastructure and AI models. It launched its flagship Qwen4-Max AI model earlier this week. In September, Alibaba's CEO called its new Zhenwu V900 chip the “most powerful” AI chip in China, while it announced massive data center investment plans in China and abroad.
Alibaba Cloud’s AI-related revenue currently comes significantly from China and there’s still a lot of “untapped demand” from Chinese enterprises, said Jacob Cooke of the Beijing-based consultancy WPIC Marketing + Technologies.
For the latest July-September quarter, Alibaba reported a 53% year-on-year revenue surge for its AI cloud and compute services to nearly 61 billion yuan ($9 billion). Total revenue for the quarter rose 10% from the year before to almost 272 billion yuan ($41 billion), slightly better than what analysts had expected.
While the company has a strong cash buffer, capital expenditures jumped 60% during the quarter to 50.5 billion yuan ($7.6 billion) thanks to its increased spending on AI infrastructure buildout.
Tencent says US chip curb ‘sets everyone back in China’
Chinese tech giant Tencent on Wednesday said the new U.S. rule on chip access “sets everyone back in China.”
“Everyone is actually having less compute, advanced compute, to work with, no matter when you actually started leasing or building capacities outside of China,” Tencent President Martin Lau said on an earnings call. Training timelines for Tencent’s next versions of its AI models would probably be impacted, he said.
“Chinese AI firms are still heavily dependent on the most frontier Nvidia chips," said James Chai, a researcher at the ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore, with new U.S. rules on remote access cutting off a huge portion of Chinese firms’ access to compute.
A study released in October by the Institute for Progress, a U.S. think tank, estimated that remote access to AI chips through overseas data centers could account for roughly one-third of China’s AI compute by the end of 2027.
Nvidia, meanwhile, said it is now “no longer shipping” chips including the H200, one of its more powerful chips, though not the most advanced, although the Trump administration greenlighted some sales to China, reflecting how Nvidia has toughened its stance on China following Huang’s ouster.
Analysts expect the U.S. will step up its chip export control policies against China after Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former senior executive of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, raised U.S. national security concerns. Earlier reporting by The New York Times suggested that U.S. officials suspected Alice Huang was a Chinese spy recruited in part to potentially influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available to Chinese companies.
Beijing has rejected claims that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy, and has called the new U.S. rules blocking Chinese companies' remote access to computing power overseas “economic coercion.”
Analysts and industry leaders in China say the U.S.’s tightening of chip export control measures would ultimately accelerate China’s push to make its domestic chip industry self-sufficient.
“Over the longer run, we believe all Chinese players would actually have to rely on domestic supply chains and domestic chips, which we actually see the industry is actually progressing very fast,” said Tencent's Lau.

articles.title_orig: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order
articles.title_zh: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order
articles.content_orig:
The U.K. government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information.
The Thursday ruling from the U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret.
The tribunal’s ruling rejected the Home Office’s claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.
The ruling comes a year after the U.K. government reportedly demanded that Apple build a backdoor to allow U.K. authorities access to customer data anywhere in the world. Details of the so-called “technical capabilities notice,” which are issued under strict non-disclosure rules, leaked to the media, which drew ire from White House officials and U.S. lawmakers who criticized the effort , arguing that the U.K. order would put Americans’ privacy at risk.
California-based Apple refused the order, and blocked U.K. users from switching on its Advanced Data Protection data-encryption feature for iCloud, rather than comply with the demand. The U.K.’s secret order was later narrowed to allow access to British nationals’ data stored in Apple’s encrypted cloud, and Apple also challenged this second order.
Prior to the ruling, Apple was legally barred from disclosing the order, even after details leaked. When reached for comment, Apple told TechCrunch that it welcomes the decision to make public the fact that the U.K. Home Office issued a technical capability notice.
Apple previously said that it has “never built a backdoor or master key” to any of its products or services and “never will.”
A spokesperson for the U.K. Home Office, which has yet to confirm the existence of a notice, did not respond to a request for comment.
Rights group Liberty International, which brought the legal challenge on behalf of two individuals, said that this is the first known time that the government has been compelled to confirm the existence of a secret technical order.
A final hearing on what specific order details can be released is anticipated next year.

Houthi rebels strike in Yemen as Middle East tensions escalate. Hudson Institute senior fellow Rebecca Heinrichs joins 'America's Newsroom' to analyze the Iran-backed proxy threat and the latest updates on the war in Ukraine.
A "terrorist attack" by the Iran-backed Houthis damaged multiple floors at the tallest skyscraper in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which houses the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund on Thursday, authorities and reports said.
Entrances leading into the King Abdullah Financial District were closed and people were being evacuated from the area following the strike by a suspected Houthi missile, according to Reuters.
The news agency reported that the attack on the Public Investment Fund Tower, which is 80 stories tall, destroyed windows across up to eight floors of the building and bent portions of its metal facade.
"One of the towers of the Financial Center in Riyadh was targeted in a terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia, causing material damage but no injuries — praise be to God," the General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defense wrote on X as it shared a photo of the damage.
HOUTHIS KILL 14 AT SAUDI AIRPORT AS EXPERT WARNS OF 'RAPID TARGETS' AMID MIDDLE EAST WAR
The Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, is the tallest skyscraper in the city. The building was seen damaged on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, following what officials called a "terrorist attack" by the Iran-backed Houthis. (General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defense)
The incident unfolded after the Houthis attacked a building belonging to Saudi state-owned oil company Aramco, in the same area on Nov. 8, Reuters reported.
Saudi-led coalition spokesman Col. Turki Al-Malki said Thursday that Saudi air defenses "intercepted and destroyed 4 ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia toward the southern region."
He also said the coalition went on offense in Yemen, destroying a ballistic missile launch platform in Dhamar that was used by the Houthis "in an attempt to attack Riydah today."
HOUTHIS EMERGE AS GLOBAL THREAT BEYOND IRAN CONTROL AMID SAUDI STRIKES, FORMER ENVOY WARNS
The KAFD World Trade Center, Riyadh Bank skyscraper office building, Public Investment Fund tower and Saudi National Bank headquarters stand beyond the King Abdullah Financial District Conference Center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Tuesday, Dec. 6, 2022. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The Houthis have been escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia during the U.S.-Iran war.
The U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Saudi Arabia warned Americans earlier this week that they "should exercise heightened vigilance due to the increased threat of armed attacks by Iranian-supported Houthis and Iranian efforts to target U.S. government officials and facilities in the region.

articles.title_orig: AMD’s China ties complicate its appeal as Nvidia’s rival.
articles.title_zh: AMD’s China ties complicate its appeal as Nvidia’s rival.
articles.content_orig:
Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices were down about 7% Wednesday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the company "has its own China problem."
Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.
The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers."
CNBC did not independently verify this information.
Hunterbrook also said that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips."
The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.
AMD did not immediately reply to a CNBC request for comment.
Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, said on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

articles.title_orig: The Best ‘GTA 6’ Gun Is Very Easy To Get From The Start
articles.title_zh: The Best ‘GTA 6’ Gun Is Very Easy To Get From The Start
articles.content_orig:
After a 13-year wait and endless memes, the time has come for gamers of all stripes to call out of work for a few days and put their noses to the Grand Theft Auto grindstone. To put this in perspective, when "Grand Theft Auto 5" came out, the Tesla Model S was the best EV you could get had a range of 265 miles. Today, the longest-range EV SUVs are pushing past 400 miles. Before you put your headphones on and play for four days straight without coming up for air, though, there's something important you should know about how Rockstar's newest game works.
Car trunks are an integral component of how you'll plan missions and play the game. Why? Turns out, they're your best tool for managing inventory while on the go. Unlike in "Grand Theft Auto 5," where you had a functionally limitless inventory and could whip out your RPG on a dime and start blasting, it's looking like inventory management is going to be a big part of the gameplay in "Grand Theft Auto 6." You start the game with a set amount of stuff you can carry on your character, whether it's Lucia or Jason, and there's no way to increase that amount over the course of the game.
That's right. There's no raising skills or buying a larger carrying capacity, like in "Cyberpunk 2077." No trading Korok seeds for more slots, like in "Breath of the Wild." And certainly no princess treatment like an infinite inventory. What you see is what you get, and what you take into a mission is all you have. Thankfully, you can stuff a limited amount of gear into your ride's rear, allowing you a little extra flexibility while out exploring Vice City in your unlicensed, legally distinct Mercedes-Benz .
Taking full advantage of your trunk's inventory is mercifully easy. You just have to find where you parked your car (you parked in a designated space, right?) and open up your trunk, just like you would in real life. You can swap out gear you're carrying with gear stashed in the trunk, or you can keep your trunk empty, unload loot into it, and get back out to where the action is with inventory slots open for further finds.
If, for some reason, you decide to commit crimes while out enjoying a drive, you can clean up your mess by stuffing bodies in the trunk, too. You wouldn't do that, though, because you're a law-abiding citizen of Vice City, not a crazed criminal stealing cars and engaging in pointless police chases .
Your usable trunk isn't just handy for extra inventory, though. It could save your skin while evading the cops. Police in "Grand Theft Auto 6" are smarter than they've ever been (in-game, not in real life, obviously). When you get into trouble with the law, police NPCs will track certain characteristics of Jason and Lucia, which helps track these criminals across the city. They'll remember details like what clothes you're wearing, what weapons you're wielding, and what car you're driving.
You'll want to carry extra weapons and a change of clothes in your extra trunk storage. That way, when you get into trouble, you can run back to your car, complete a magical-girl transformation into your new outfit, and lower the likelihood that you'll get caught. Be careful, though. GTA 6 has Flock-like cameras that track your character's movements , and you'll have to stop at gas stations to fuel up virtually . So much for gaming being a break from reality.
GTA 6's usable trunk system promises to make the gameplay more dynamic and more challenging in fun ways, and it's a big departure from what franchise fans will be used to from "Grand Theft Auto 4" and "Grand Theft Auto 5." However, this isn't a completely original idea.
In fact, this is actually a reprise of a similar mechanic from an earlier Rockstar game. "L.A. Noire" is a 2011 neo-noir mystery game that also used a storage system that involved the trunk of the player character's car. Like GTA, "L.A. Noire" also features plenty of car chases and guns, though you play as a detective named Cole Phelps and try to solve crimes rather than commit them.
You may also remember a similar mechanic from the critically acclaimed and award-winning 2018 game "Red Dead Redemption 2." In "Red Dead Redemption 2," main character Arthur Morgan keeps a saddle on his horse that functions as additional storage. Much like in "Grand Theft Auto 6," returning to your horse allowed you to dig through your saddlebags and pull out both weapons and clothes, which are used to evade enemies and equip the different outfits needed for different weather.
For better or worse, inventory management is frequently one of the stickiest parts of game design, and it can make or break a game. Let's all cross our fingers extra hard that "Grand Theft Auto 6" nails the trunk storage mechanics and that changing your clothes in your car isn't a total drag like it is in real life.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine strikes Putin’s prized Crimean bridge for third time in a week
articles.title_zh: Ukraine strikes Putin’s prized Crimean bridge for third time in a week
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for the third time in a week, forcing a suspension of train services across it, Russian authorities said, hours before President Vladimir Putin met the leaders of China and the U.S.
The timing and impact of Ukraine‘s attacks on the bridge, the longest in Europe and a symbol of Putin’s Russia, are awkward for the Kremlin chief as he participates in what Moscow has cast as a historic trilateral summit with President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping .
Moscow hopes the meeting will send a signal to allies and foes that it — rather than the European Union and Britain — is part of an emerging new multilateral world order.
There was no immediate comment on the latest attack from Ukraine or Volodymyr Zelenskyy , its president, who was due to hold talks in Berlin later on Thursday with U.S. peace envoys.
Sergei Aksyonov, Crimea’s Russian-installed governor, issued a defiant video message in which he said rail travel across the bridge would resume later on Thursday.
“We have the strength, the resolve and the understanding of how to resolve this situation. We will overcome everything. Crimea is with Russia forever!” Aksyonov said.
In a statement, Russia’s transport ministry said that nobody had been hurt in the latest Ukrainian attack on the Black Sea peninsula, which Moscow annexed from Ukraine in 2014 , and that specialists were assessing damage to the bridge.
The 12-mile bridge is a flagship project that Putin inaugurated in 2018 and that symbolizes Russia’s attachment to the peninsula, which is also the home of its Black Sea Fleet, whose ships Ukraine has repeatedly targeted.
On Tuesday, Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, forcing its main road arch to crumble into the sea while leaving a yawning gap, according to videos and images verified by Reuters, dealing a military and symbolic blow to Russia.
That attack is likely to make it harder for Russia to keep up supplies to the peninsula, which is home to nearly 2.5 million people, and is likely to put pressure on Russian military logistics in parts of southern Ukraine held by Moscow’s forces.
This week‘s first attack, on Monday, caused more minor damage to the bridge.

Ahead of launch, Rockstar Games mentioned that instead of including a map inside the physical edition of GTA 6 , they'd be making it available to download for free on their website, as well as providing a double-sided physical edition.
The downloadable version is now officially available for free on the GTA 6 website , and there's even a special "printable" option for those who don't just want to look at it in digital form.
It comes with a big version of the GTA 6 cover art as well - you can see both of these down below:
The physical edition still isn't available yet, but Rockstar Games says that it will be "made available at the Rockstar Store shortly after launch". We'll keep an eye out and update this article when that happens.
Honestly, I don't think the map is that great, as I hoped it might include things like store and minigame locations rather than just each area that's available to visit, but as a poster on a wall, it's definitely still worth displaying somewhere.
I'd rather wait for the physical version, but it's certainly nice that it exists as a freebie as well.

articles.title_orig: Social Security raise: What’s left after the Medicare premium hike?
articles.title_zh: Social Security raise: What’s left after the Medicare premium hike?
articles.content_orig:

https://money.com/medicare-part-b-adjustment-2027-social-security/
More on Retirement from Pete
More on Retirement from Julia
Next year's Social Security payments will rise thanks to the cost-of-living adjustment , but a newly announced Medicare premium hike will eat into recipients' raises.
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced Tuesday that the standard Medicare Part B premium will increase by $6.50, or 3.2%, for 2027.
More than 70 million people are covered by Medicare, the government health insurance program for Americans 65 and older and younger people with certain disabilities or conditions. About 64 million have both Medicare Part A, the hospital insurance that is premium-free for most people, and Medicare Part B, which covers physician services and outpatient care.
The standard Medicare Part B premium will increase from $202.90 per month in 2026 to $209.40 per month in 2027, according to the announcement.
Most Part B enrollees pay the standard Part B premium, while about 8% who have higher incomes pay more. Some lower-income enrollees have their premiums covered by Medicaid or state-administered Medicare Savings Programs.
Here is a breakdown of Medicare Part B premiums, including the income-related monthly adjustment amount, or IRMAA, for higher earners:
The surcharges for high earners are typically based on modified adjusted gross income from 2025 tax returns, under a two-year lookback rule. Enrollees may be able to request that the government use more current information if they've recently gone through a "life-changing event" such as retirement, divorce or the death of a spouse.
Medicare Part B premiums are automatically deducted from an individual's Social Security benefits, though some enrollees are billed directly. A common example would be a Medicare beneficiary who is waiting until the full retirement age, 67, or later to claim their retirement benefits through Social Security.
The Medicare Part B increase will effectively offset part of the boost in Social Security benefits that folks will receive under the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment, or COLA. On Oct. 14, the Social Security Administration announced that the COLA is 3.6%, set to take effect in January for most Social Security recipients. It will raise the average retirement benefit by about $75 per month.
This year's increase in the standard Medicare Part B premium is smaller than last year's adjustment of $17.90, which was the second-largest in the program's history. Unlike the COLA, the Medicare Part B premium is not an inflation adjustment. Medicare adjustments are calculated using rules laid out in the Social Security Act that state that the premium must cover about 25% of projected costs for beneficiaries 65 and older.
According to CMS, "the increase in the 2027 Part B standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending."
CMS also announced the new full Medicare Part A premium, which will be $597 per month in 2027, up from $565 this year. Keep in mind that Medicare Part A premiums are only paid by about 1% of Medicare enrollees — namely, those who have not paid Medicare taxes for 40 quarters.
The reduced Medicare Part A premium, which applies to people who are close to the work requirement with at least 30 quarters of coverage (and their spouses), will be $328 per month next year, up from $311.
In Tuesday's release, CMS also announced the new Medicare Part A and Part B deductibles for 2027. (The deductibles are the amount you owe before Medicare starts paying its share.)
The Part A inpatient hospital deductible will rise from $1,736 to $1,776, a $40 increase. This deductible covers up to 60 days of a hospital stay in a benefit period.
After that point, patients owe a coinsurance amount: $444 per day in 2027 for the 61st through 90th days and $888 for "lifetime reserve" days, which can cover the 91st through 150th days of a stay. Beyond that, the costs fall entirely on the patient.
The Part B deductible will rise to $292 in 2027, up from $283 this year. Once the deductible is met, Medicare generally covers 80% of the cost of approved services, while Part B enrollees pay a 20% coinsurance share.

articles.title_zh: Thanksgiving dinner will come with higher price tag: Research
articles.content_orig:
For the first time since 2022, American shoppers will see an increase in the price of goods for Thanksgiving dinner. Results from the American Farm Bureau Federation's 41st annual Thanksgiving dinner cost survey indicate that the price of a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 people averages $58.63, up 6% from a year ago.
Over Four Decades of AFBF Thanksgiving Surveys
Each November, as millions of Americans prepare to gather with their family and friends to celebrate Thanksgiving, hundreds of volunteer shoppers from all 50 states and Puerto Rico participate in AFBF's annual Thanksgiving dinner cost survey. Every year since 1986, shoppers have reported prices for a standard list of items at their local grocery store for a variety of ingredients used to craft Thanksgiving favorites. Up until 2018, the survey included carrots, celery, cranberries, cubed stuffing, dinner rolls, frozen green peas, sweet potatoes, pumpkin pie mix, frozen pie crusts, whole milk, heavy whipping cream, and the ubiquitous American holiday staple: turkey. In 2018, AFBF added ham, frozen green beans and russet potatoes to better reflect the price of an all-American Thanksgiving meal.
While the overall cost of Thanksgiving dinner ticked upward in 2026, prices for several items included in the survey decreased slightly from 2025. A vegetable tray containing celery and carrots posted the largest percentage decline in this year's survey, with a 3.7% decrease compared to a year ago. In terms of absolute dollar changes, frozen pie crusts had the sharpest decrease, posting a decrease of 9 cents compared to a year ago. The survey bodes well for pumpkin pie enthusiasts, who will enjoy a lower overall cost for their beloved dessert despite an increase in the cost of pumpkin pie mix, as heavy whipping cream is also cheaper in 2026 compared to last year.
Higher Prices for Several Thanksgiving Favorites
The overall cost of a 10-person Thanksgiving dinner increased for 2026, largely fueled by increases in items key to the Turkey Day menu. The most notable increase for 2026 is the turkey itself, with the average price of a 16 pound frozen bird being $23.68, an increase of $2.38 (10%) from 2025. As discussed in a recent Farm Bureau Intel , strong demand and tight inventories have led to increased prices for turkey in 2026.
Apart from turkey, other widely featured Thanksgiving items increased in this year's survey. Grocery store prices for boneless ham, milk, dinner rolls, sweet potatoes, russet potatoes, frozen peas, frozen green beans, cranberries, and cubed stuffing (known in some regions as “dressing”) all increased in 2026.
Higher prices for these items aren't a complete surprise, as the effects of significant spikes in prices for critical inputs throughout the supply chain, like fuel for processing and transportation, have made their way to consumers. America's farmers and ranchers also face significant challenges, with record diesel costs, elevated fertilizer prices, increased labor expenses, and a bigger bill for items like rent and electricity — all of which hurt their ability to breakeven at the end of the year. However, unlike wholesalers and retailers, farmers aren’t able to pass those costs up the supply chain
Thanksgiving Dinner Prices Vary Across the Country
At an average of $61.57 for a 10-person classic Thanksgiving dinner, the Northeast has the highest cost. The Northeast's dinner basket cost is about 5% higher than the national average.  The average cost for a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 in the West and Midwest is closer to the national average, at $58.74 and $56.89, respectively. The South's average dinner cost is $54.33.
Some Shoppers May Find Great Deals
Despite the overall increase in the average cost of Thanksgiving dinner this year, some of our shoppers were able to find staggering deals on a variety of items, including turkey, which some shoppers reported finding  for as low as 69 cents per pound, nearly half the average nationwide price for a pound of turkey.  As Thanksgiving approaches, shoppers will look for deals on a variety of items to bring down the cost of their Thanksgiving dinner grocery list.
Higher Grocery Prices Do Not Mean Higher Farm Profits
Farm Bureau's 2026 Thanksgiving Dinner market basket survey indicates that Americans will pay more to feed family and friends this Thanksgiving. Nearly all items surveyed increased in price compared to 2025, with turkey, milk and cranberries posting some of the largest year-over-year percentage gains. However, higher grocery prices do not necessarily translate into better returns for America's farmers and ranchers.
Farmers and ranchers are largely price-takers, not price-makers, and receive only a small share of what consumers spend at the grocery store. USDA's Food Dollar Series estimates that less than 6 cents of every dollar spent on food goes back to the farm. Even when higher retail prices translate into increased farm revenue, rising production costs can quickly offset those gains. Elevated prices for critical inputs such as diesel, fertilizer and equipment continue to squeeze farm margins.
For example, this year's survey found that a 12-ounce bag of cranberries costs nearly 9% more than last year. That increase does not necessarily mean the Wisconsin cranberry farmer who grew them is receiving a higher price. Even if the farmer does capture some additional revenue, those earnings are needed to cover increased fertilizer, fuel and other production expenses.
As Americans gather around the Thanksgiving table, it's important to remember that higher food prices can place pressure on both consumers and the farmers who produce that food. Wherever and however you celebrate this Thanksgiving, take a moment to thank America's farmers and ranchers, who continue working through challenging economic conditions to provide the food, fuel and fiber we rely on every day.

articles.title_orig: Stocks making the biggest moves Thursday: Palo Alto Networks, Take-Two Interactive, Everpure, Walmart & more
articles.title_zh: Stocks making the biggest moves Thursday: Palo Alto Networks, Take-Two Interactive, Everpure, Walmart & more
articles.content_orig:
Palo Alto Networks popped in early trading Thursday, boosted by quarterly results that beat analyst expectations. AMD, meanwhile, tumbled on the back of a short seller report.
Follow along as CNBC covers the biggest stock market moves of the day.
Neocloud CoreWeave gained 1% on enthusiasm from the Anthropic IPO plus a change in Texas permitting that favors data center development.
Texas officials started issuing air permits again for data center construction projects, according to Reuters , which bodes well for the future of the physical component of the AI buildout.
Nvidia's highly anticipated earnings call earlier this week also offered clarity on the leadership direction for the firm, which Wall Street analysts responded positively to. Analysts at Truist were encouraged on Tuesday by Nvidia statements on the call about its relationship to neoclouds.
"Notably, NVIDIA's earnings commentary … [described] neoclouds as an 'increasingly important' part of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem and stating that it will continue working with and supporting leading neocloud partners, while becoming more disciplined and selective in that support."
AMD shares tumbled more than 9% after Hunterbrook Capital revealed it took a short position on the company.
In a post titled "AMD has its own China problem", Hunterbrook alleges that "AMD firmware keeps turning up at a blacklisted Chinese company and three companies tied to it, just as U.S. export restrictions are scheduled to expand."
"AMD, which bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong, also depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips," Hunterbrook added.
CNBC reached out to AMD for comment.
Shares of Coherent are up nearly 11%, extending gains after Nvidia 's latest earnings report earlier in the week highlighted continued demand for data-center technology.
Coherent, which supplies optical components used in AI data centers, said its data-center revenue rose 85% year over year in its fiscal first quarter.
On Nov. 18, the company's board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $2 billion . Coherent may buy shares in the open market or through other transactions. The program has no expiration date and does not require the company to repurchase a specific amount.
Shares of the software company making tools for computer chips jumped 3.2% after Barclays initiated coverage with an overweight rating and a $640 price target implying 47% upside from Wednesday's close. Analyst Saket Kalia noted that Synopsys is the leader of a growing Electronic Design Automation (EDA) market, which is driven by rising spend in semiconductor research and development.
MongoDB gained 4% before the bell following an upgrade at UBS to buy from neutral.
The bank's channel checks pointed to steady demand and better-than-expected consumer and partner growth, which should support durable 20%-plus total revenue growth and 25%-plus revenue growth for its cloud database service Atlas over the coming years, analyst Radi Sultan said.
In addition, MongoDB could be utilized in 20% to 40% of incremental AI workloads, which is not fully reflected in the stock's valuation, he said.
Data storage stocks are getting a lift in the premarket Thursday as the Anthropic IPO aims to breathe new life into AI-trade
Shares of Seagate Technology are up more than 6% while Western Digital stock popped 5.8%.
Seagate and Western Digital provide provide mass data storage infrastructure, a crucial role in the AI ecosystem to help AI models run.
The strong momentum around data storage and AI infrastructure demand is already high.
But a large chuck of that demand will come from leading AI lab Anthropic, which is set to go public Thursday.
Chipmakers advanced on Thursday ahead of Anthropic's IPO.
Marvell gained 4.2%, Advanced Micro Devices is up 2.8%, Broadcom advanced 2.5%, Intel moved 4.4% higher and Nvidia is up 1.5%.
These artificial intelligence chips will help Anthropic run Claude models faster.
Leading chipmakers need the IPO to go well, as Anthropic has $900 billion in spending commitments.
Shares of Bloom Energy surged nearly 8% in the premarket Thursday after being upgraded to outperform at BMO Capital Markets.
The analysts cited their endorsement of the company after coming away with positive meetings with management.
The firm however decreased its price target to $230 from $260, which still implies a 35% upside to the stock's Thursday close of $170 per share.
UBS upgraded the intelligent content management provider to buy from neutral, sending shares 3.6% higher in premarket trading.
The firm believes Box 's recent artificial intelligence growth acceleration can support sustained double-digit revenue growth. "Investors have been looking for evidence that AI can drive an inflection in software growth, and Box is increasingly demonstrating exactly that," analyst Taylor McGinnis wrote.
Walmart shares were down more than 1% even after the retail giant reported third-quarter results that beat expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The company posted adjusted earnings per share of 65 cents on revenue of $188.84 billion. Analysts expected a profit of 64 cents per share on revenue of $187.27 billion.
For the year, Walmart sees net sales rising 4.9% to 5.2%, more than a previous guidance of 4% to 5%.
Shares of Take-Two Interactive slipped 1%, giving back some of their gains from the previous session. The stock popped more than 6% on Wednesday ahead of the release of the much-anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" game.
Take-Two is up nearly 14% in November, though the stock has dropped 15% in 2026.
Cybersecurity player Palo Alto Networks advanced 10% after its fiscal first-quarter results came in above the Street's expectations.
The company earned $1.05 per share on an adjusted basis and revenue of $3.44 billion. The LSEG consensus estimate called for 97 cents per share on $3.31 billion of revenue.
Guidance for the fiscal year ending July 2027 calls for adjusted earnings of $4.26 to $4.30 per share on revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion. Analysts sought $4.18 per share and $14.16 billion, according to LSEG.
The data management company advanced 5% after raising its guidance for the fiscal-year ending January 2027.
Everpure sees revenue in a range of $5.20 billion to $5.21 billion, up from its earlier call of $5.03 billion to $5.07 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for $5.06 billion.
Third-quarter results also surpassed estimates on the top and bottom lines.
The manufacturer of power generation equipment pulled back 1%. Woodward expects adjusted earnings for the fiscal year ending September 2027 to range between $10.20 and $10.70 per share, below the FactSet consensus estimate of $10.74 per share.

articles.title_orig: Walmart raises full-year outlook as wealthier shoppers fuel sales growth
articles.title_zh: Walmart raises full-year outlook as wealthier shoppers fuel sales growth
articles.content_orig:
Walmart on Thursday reported earnings and revenue that narrowly topped estimates and raised its full-year outlook as it saw strong e-commerce growth ahead of the busy holiday season.
Walmart said global e-commerce sales grew 17%, driven by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, with Walmart U.S. up 23% and Sam's Club U.S. rising 30%. Its Walmart U.S. advertising business saw a 37% sales increase for the quarter.
Walmart said it rolled back prices on nearly 8,000 products across its stores, a focus as U.S. consumers worry about the cost of living in the face of elevated food and gas prices.
CEO John Furner told CNBC's Becky Quick that the company has seen higher-than-expected diesel costs, but that tariff refunds have helped the retailer to offset those inputs and maintain lower prices.
"The reality is that increases in diesel fuel and transportation, they do work their way into cost of goods," Furner said in an exclusive interview. "So we're hoping to see these costs come down as soon as possible, and we'll keep prices as low as we can."
CFO John David Rainey told CNBC that growth in online orders for Walmart and Sam's Club was driven by an emphasis on speed of delivery and reduced prices. He added that Walmart saw its largest share gains in the food category in three years during the third quarter.
"This was another really solid quarter for us, we feel good about it," Rainey told CNBC. "We continue to gain share while continuing to improve the profitability of our digital businesses."
Walmart also raised its full-year guidance, now expecting net sales to rise between 4.9% and 5.2%, compared to previous guidance of a 4% to 5% increase. Rainey said Walmart is maintaining "flexibility" in its guidance.
Walmart anticipates adjusted earnings per share will come in between $2.84 and $2.89, compared with a prior range of $2.80 to $2.87. It's also now expecting adjusted operating income to increase between 8% and 8.6%, up from the previous outlook of between 7% and 8.5% growth.
Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
For the quarter ended Oct. 31, the company reported net income of $4.95 billion, or 62 cents per share, down from $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share, the year prior. Revenue rose 5.2%.
Walmart U.S. recorded net sales of $125 billion, up 3.6% from the year prior. Its comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.9%, in line with Wall Street expectations, according to StreetAccount.
Furner also said Walmart is seeing encouraging adoption of its artificial intelligence agent, named Sparky, especially ahead of the holiday season. He said it's led to customer basket increases of 40% on average.
"It just is a great way of just completing the entire basket and solving entire the solution for people," he said.
Sam's Club reported net sales of $25.9 billion, marking a 10% increase from the year-ago period. It said its sales were driven by strength in the grocery category and general merchandise.
In October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with Walmart+ and Sam's Club as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer standalone memberships, as well.
Furner told CNBC the new membership has brought roughly two million new people into Sam's Club since its launch in late October. Though the company reimbursed some members for the new membership rate, Rainey added it's already seeing positive returns on the joint model and that consumers are "spending appreciably more."
The company on Thursday said its global membership fee revenue grew 17% in the third quarter.
The company is typically well-insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter , the company said it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef.
Rainey said on Thursday that he's "optimistic" about consumer spending heading into the holiday season and that the fourth quarter is already "off to a pretty good start."
The big-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership.
Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year-to-date.

articles.title_orig: China and Russia say they and US agree on UN reforms, boosting fuel supplies, dialogue on nuclear
articles.title_zh: China and Russia say they and US agree on UN reforms, boosting fuel supplies, dialogue on nuclear
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has repeatedly placed nonproliferation near the top of the agenda for his trilateral meeting Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin , although his counterparts have expressed little interest in committing to new limitations on their nuclear arsenals.
Trump has been pushing for China to join the U.S. and Russia in a new nuclear arms control agreement since his first term in office. Still, he has sought to limit expectations for any major progress in Shenzhen, China, where the world’s top three nuclear powers are meeting on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders .
Russia suspended its participation in New START, its last remaining nuclear arms pact with the U.S., when it invaded Ukraine in 2022, denying inspections of its nuclear sites. Ahead of the treaty’s expiration this past February , Russia said it would keep to the deal’s limitations on its arsenal for another year, but Trump insisted a new agreement must include China and possibly other nuclear powers.
China has said an arms control agreement should remain between the U.S. and Russia, which together hold nearly 90% of the world’s nuclear arsenal with more than 5,000 warheads each. China has about 600, according to Pentagon estimates, though by 2030 it could have up to 1,000 if its arsenal continues to expand at the current rate.
“China is building up its nuclear arsenal to a very significant degree, and it will continue to do so, and wants to continue to do so,” David Sacks, a senior fellow for Asia studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, told reporters Wednesday.
The Chinese foreign ministry has declined to say whether nuclear arms control will be discussed at the trilateral meeting on Thursday, with spokesperson Mao Ning saying earlier this week that the three leaders “will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace.”
In a call last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi “agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearization,” according to a U.S. readout of the call. The Chinese readout made no reference to such a discussion.
Trump has admitted that it will be difficult to get Russia and China to consider reducing their nuclear arsenals.
“So we’re going to talk about denuclearization. Tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes, right? But especially since you do have other countries,” he said Monday. “But we’re going to be talking about denuclearization.”
Even in the hours leading up to this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, the world’s top two nuclear powers were making shows of force. On Tuesday, the U.S. launched an unarmed intercontinental ballistic missile in a previously unannounced test at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Hours later, Russia landed two strategic bombers in Vietnam to coincide with Putin’s arrival in China.
While one meeting is not likely to produce dramatic breakthroughs, it could kickstart a process that leads to sustained, formal bilateral or multilateral negotiations on nuclear risk reduction, arms control and disarmament, said Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Washington-based Arms Control Association.
“A top priority for all three leaders should be to head off a costly, escalatory nuclear arms race involving the further buildup of nuclear forces and the resumption of nuclear testing by any state,” he said.
Da Wei, director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, said nuclear arms control was not a “proper topic” for the trilateral meeting given the complexity of the issue and how little time Trump, Putin and Xi will have together.
But if the three leaders “can say something about nuclear stability, like a nuclear war is not winnable and should not be fought, I think that will be helpful,” he said in an interview Wednesday.
Rubio has acknowledged that a new agreement could take some time.
“Past agreements, including New START, took years to negotiate and were built upon decades of precedent. They were also between two powers, not three or more,” he wrote on Substack in February. “However, just because something is hard does not mean we should not pursue it or settle for less.”
Abigail Williams is a producer and reporter for NBC News covering the State Department.

articles.content_orig:
