articles.title_orig: What the Crimean bridge attack means for Russia
articles.title_zh: What the Crimean bridge attack means for Russia
articles.content_orig:
It had been a year and a half since Ukraine last attacked the 19-kilometer-long Kerch Bridge connecting Russian-annexed Crimea with Russia's Krasnodar region.
Now, Ukraine has struck again. The attack during the night of November 17 caused the highway section of the bridge to collapse into the sea. As a result, shipping traffic between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov has also been disrupted.
Russia's ministry of transport announced a "temporary suspension" of road and rail traffic on the bridge, though later, rail services were resumed. Russian authorities have launched a criminal investigation into what they are calling a "terrorist attack." It was only after this announcement that the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) confirmed the attack.
The Kerch Strait bridge is considered one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's most prestigious projects. Its construction began after Russia's 2014 annexation of the Ukrainian Crimea peninsula , an act considered illegal under international law. The Kerch Bridge was completed four years later.
It has been targeted by Ukraine on several occasions since Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion . The most well-known strike occurred in October 2022, when an explosives-laden truck detonated on the bridge, causing extensive damage and several months of traffic restrictions. The most recent attack took place in June 2025, when the SBU reported that an underwater support structure was blown up.
The latest Ukrainian operation lasted about a month, and consisted of seven distinct phases. "First, the SBU and armed forces systematically neutralized the enemy's air defense system. After that, the direct attack on the bridge began," says the SBU Telegram channel.
Some Russian military bloggers claim that the attack was carried out with the support of Ukraine's Western allies, or at least using their equipment and weapons.
Ukraine has not confirmed this. It has instead pointed out that various Ukrainian-made weapons were used in the attack, ranging from a variety of drones, to FP-5 Flamingo and R-360 Neptun missiles. British daily The Times has cited Ukrainian military sources, saying that Ukraine attacked the bridge without the support of SpaceX's satellite network system Starlink . There has been no confirmation of this so far.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , meanwhile, described the strike as a response to Russian attacks: "Russia is attacking our infrastructure every day, particularly bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region." He said "we are rebuilding our infrastructure, but we also remind Russia that the war always returns to where it began."
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
After the attack, pictures and videos of the bridge were shared on social media. The Krimskij Veter Telegram channel has highlighted damage to the railroad link and questioned why Russian authorities have opted to resume train services.
The Kerch Strait shipping channel is also completely blocked by debris. "This brings road traffic to a standstill, but also shipping between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov," the channel writes.
Indeed, the Kerch Strait navigational channel is merely 120 meters wide, writes Mychajlo Hontschar of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies "Strategy XXI" on Facebook. "The strait is shallow, only three to five meters deep."
As early as the 19th century, the seabed was dredged to allow heavier ships to pass from the Black Sea to the Sea of Azov and vice versa. "Now, Vladimir Putin's bridge-building efforts have brought shipping to an indefinite standstill," Hontschar said.
Not only will river-sea vessels no longer be able to leave the waters of the Sea of Azov, the Don, and the Volga, but boats and small ships from the Black Sea fleet and the Caspian flotilla based in Novorossiysk will also be unable to do so.
Many pro-Kremlin Telegram channels have been quick to claim that the bridge does not play an important role in the Russian army's logistics or in supplying Crimea.
The Dva Mayora (Two Majors) channel quotes the "Deputy President of the Republic of Crimea," Olga Kurlayeva, who described the bridge as a "purely civilian structure."
Ukrainian military experts interviewed by DW, on the other hand, point to the systematic disruption of Russian logistics. These efforts also included regular attacks on the R-80 highway leading through Russian-occupied territories of the Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson regions.
Russia cannot replace the Kerch Bridge with any other land connection, says Oleksandr Kovalenko, a Ukrainian military expert with the Information Resistance Group that seeks to counter disinformation. He expects the damaged bridge will cause supply problems for the Russian armed forces: "If there is a resource shortage during attacks or in defense, then either the attacks or the defense will fail."
That is why he does not rule out a decline in attacks from occupied Crimea on the rest of Ukraine. "There are many launch pads for kamikaze drones in Crimea — in the Hvardijsk area, at Cape Chauda and in Balaklava," Kovalenko told DW. "From there, many drones are launched toward Odesa, Mykolaiv, and the right bank of the Dnipro River in the Kherson region. They also fly over Crimea en route toward Ukraine. Then there are attacks using Iskander-M ballistic missiles, as well as Zircon and Oniks missiles, guided missiles, and glide bombs. And while they don't originate in Crimea, they are brought over via the Kerch Bridge."
Kovalenko says the bridge strike has dealt a serious blow to Vladimir Putin's standing. It comes at a sensitive time as Putin is about to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, China .
Memes and witty comments about the bridge abound on X. Meanwhile, the Russian president's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov has promised to rebuild the bridge and assured that it will be "even better than before."
Andrii Korezkyj of the Kyiv University of Transportation, however, says this is not likely to happen anytime soon. "All in all, I would estimate that it would take between one and a half and three years [to rebuild]," Korezkyj told DW, adding, "I don't think they'll let the Russians build another [bridge] arch like that near the Ukrainian border without interference."
Pro-Russian commentators, known as Z-bloggers, agree with this view. "Unlike in 2022 and 2023, the Ukrainian armed forces are now able to launch strikes against floating cranes and repair teams."
"Even installing a pre-assembled arch under these conditions would constitute a challenging task," writes the pro-Kremlin Rybar Telegram channel.
This article was translated from German.

articles.title_orig: Crew unaware of risks before Bayesian yacht accident, say investigators
articles.title_zh: Crew unaware of risks before Bayesian yacht accident, say investigators
articles.content_orig:
The crew of the Bayesian superyacht did not know about a critical safety risk that left it vulnerable in powerful winds before it sank off the coast in northern Sicily coast, killing seven people, British investigators say.
British tech tycoon Mike Lynch, 59, and his daughter Hannah, 18, were among seven people who died when the vessel sank on 19 August 2024 .
The sinking of the Bayesian unfolded with "extraordinary speed" when a violent downburst of freak hurricane-force winds knocked it onto its side in less than 15 seconds, the UK's Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) final report said.
Safety information provided to the crew did not identify this type of risk, the MAIB said.
"It was very dynamic, very quick," said MAIB principal inspector Simon Graves. "The speed of events overtook the crew and prevented them from taking any other action."
In addition to Mike Lynch, 59, the accident led to the deaths of his daughter Hannah, 18, Morgan Stanley International bank chairman Jonathan Bloomer, 70, and his wife, Judy, 71.
An American lawyer, Chris Morvillo, 59, and his wife Neda Morvillo, 57, also died, along with crew member Rick Thomas , 59.
Rob Loder, chief inspector of marine accidents said: "Our thoughts remain with the families and loved ones of the seven who lost their lives, and with all those affected by the loss of Bayesian. This accident developed with extraordinary speed."
Fifteen survivors escaped from the 56-metre (184m) luxury yacht and managed to get to a life raft that had been launched by a crew member.
The marine investigation found that the Bayesian "had a vulnerability to high winds that was not recognised, because the yacht had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down".
In addition, "the extreme winds that night were also not explicitly forecast, so the crew had no warning of the risk", Loder added.
In the early hours of 19 August 2024 the Bayesian was anchored outside of Porticello port, on the north coast of Sicily.
With thunderstorms rapidly coming in, wind speeds went from 8 knots to about 70 knots (80mph) within minutes. The weather forecast had only predicted gusts of up to 27 knots (31mph).
The MAIB report stated that with no sails set Bayesian was vulnerable to being knocked over in severe winds.
A study commissioned by the MAIB indicated that, in the conditions assessed, Bayesian was vulnerable to extreme winds at the vessels widest point, known as the beam.
It also found that any knockdown - where the boat was suddenly tipped sideways - would be "irrecoverable once the yacht passed the angle of vanishing stability", assessed in the study as being 73 degrees. Once the vessel passed this angle it could not right itself.
In addition, the centreboard, which provides stability when a ship is under sail, was raised. The report said the centreboard was not needed when the Bayesian was using its motors and was rarely lowered at anchor. The way the boat was loaded, and the angle of the wind, also contributed to the accident.
Inspectors said a "downburst of hurricane-force winds" was the most likely cause of the ship keeling over.
They happen when cold, dense air plunges rapidly, sending out violent winds across the surface.
The MAIB said that none of risks were covered in the UK training syllabus, nor in published guidance available to crew.
Once the vessel was on its side, it rapidly filled with water and sank.
The MAIB's final report into the sinking, published on Thursday, appeared to contrast with recent reports from Italy, where prosecution experts have reportedly blamed errors by the crew rather than problems with the yacht.
The investigation was carried out alongside a criminal probe in Italy , where captain James Cutfield, chief engineer Tim Parker Eaton and deckhand Matthew Griffith are under investigation over potential charges of multiple manslaughter and culpable shipwreck.
British investigators said that Italian prosecutors had restricted access to some witnesses and evidence.
"It is possible that the circumstances depicted in this report may alter following disclosure of evidence withheld by the Italian authorities," the report says.
However, the MAIB's Graves said he was satisfied with the British investigation.
"We are content with our investigation, the investigation that we've undertaken, and the information we've used to feed into it."
The report also found that alcohol consumption had not contributed to the sinking.
The MAIB report makes seven recommendations to four agencies. It calls for new regulations to be set for single-hulled sailing vessels, and new rules around life rafts.
It also urges collaboration between the Met Office and its global counterpart to improve information-sharing of severe weather forecasts with mariners.
The Maritime and Coastguard Agency is also investigating the sinking.

Anthropic's shares will start trading publicly on Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
The artificial intelligence company Anthropic said on Wednesday it sold more than 956 million shares at a price of $83 a piece in a record-breaking initial public offering that makes it one of the most valuable companies in the world.
The five-year-old AI powerhouse raised around $79.4 billion through the offering, exceeding the $75 billion IPO haul of Elon Musk's SpaceX earlier this year. Anthropic said in a statement that "certain stockholders" also sold more than 23 million shares as part of the IPO, bringing the total haul to more than $81.3 billion.
Anthropic's shares will start trading publicly on Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.
The listing was oversubscribed, despite coming at a time of growing concern about a possible AI bubble and volatility in tech stocks.
The number of shares sold and the price exceeded Anthropic's original expectations. The listing prospectus targeted a sale of 825 million shares at $70 to $78 per share.
Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR.

articles.title_orig: Trump, Xi and Putin Will Sit Down for the First Time. It Won’t Be Like Yalta.
articles.title_zh: Trump, Xi and Putin Will Sit Down for the First Time. It Won’t Be Like Yalta.
articles.content_orig:
Leaders of the US, China and Russia to take part in their first trilateral, with developments on trade, AI and global conflicts closely watched
Xi Jinping rallies against protectionism as he welcomes Trump to Apec summit
What is Apec? Explained in 30 seconds
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec), taking place today in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.
It’s a big day for global diplomacy, with a hotly anticipated meeting between US president Donald Trump, China’s leader Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin .
It is the first time ever the three leaders have held trilateral talks – with the meeting even drawing comparisons to the 1945 Yalta meeting, shorthand for great-power deals imposed on smaller countries.
On the agenda is Russia’s war with Ukraine , the US war in Iran , as well as global trade, AI, and nuclear weapons .
Speculation also abounds about the possible appearance of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un , with Trump saying he is open to engagement.
Stay tuned for an exciting day in global affairs.
Along with the coterie of world leaders at Apec , hundreds of business leaders are also in Shenzhen, with executives from BYD, Baidu, Boeing and Google set to attend .
Elon Musk is also expected to be there, along with Visa CEO Ryan ⁠McInerney, Mastercard CEO Michael Miebach and Deloitte CEO Joe Ucuzoglu.
Despite the high-profile roster of names, Nikkei Asia has reported that the number of prominent US executives appears “relatively light” compared to previous years. One official told the publication that executives had not been provided with clear agendas in advance and many were caught up in scheduling conflicts.
One major name present at the event in South Korea last year, but noticeably absent from this year’s summit, is Jensen Huang, who resigned from Nvidia last week after a scandal over an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China.
South China Morning Post reports that the chaos that has engulfed the chipmaker in the last week has played a role in discouraging some US business leaders from attending the summit, as they “worry about being perceived as close to China”.
Zak Dychtwald, the founder of BridgeWorks Global, a China-based consultancy told the paper that “CEOs had spent the last 18 months returning to China with more confidence, and this sets that back”.
Here’s the Guardian’s Rebecca Bailey on Xi Jinping’s speech today, in which she writes that he reiterated themes of openness and innovation emphasised throughout the summit.
“China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation,” he said. He announced China would give US$20 million in funding “to support APEC’s practical cooperation”, and would establish a Apec-focused research centre in Shenzhen.
“Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalisation, and reduce barriers to trade and investment,” he said.
The region should promote connectivity and innovation, he added. Green energy, energy and food security and digital infrastructure were all among areas mentioned for more coordination and collaboration.
Toward the beginning of his speech he had this poetic flourish:
double quotation mark Members of Apec are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other.
President Trump has shared some of of his thoughts on AI saying that Apec opposes regulation that would “stifle” the industry.
“We won’t allow that to happen,” he said.
Commenting on concerns about AI, the US president said:
double quotation mark It’s almost completely good, but it’s got some bad elements and we have to be very careful” in managing the bad.
Trump said his meeting on Thursday with Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin was already a “win” before it took place, Reuters news reports.
The unprecedented diplomatic gathering of the leaders of the world’s largest nuclear ⁠powers is unlikely to produce major agreements , analysts ⁠say, while it unnerves smaller countries that ​fear their interests might be disregarded.
Xi greeted Trump at the airport , ⁠the first time he has done so with any visiting leader since becoming president, reciprocating his counterpart’s gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September when they last met. The leaders also briefly hugged.
double quotation mark This is a great president, one of the great presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody,” Trump ⁠said, when asked what he wanted to get out of the unprecedented three-way meet.
And not only that, the fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people, the young children, the soldiers, the whole thing. ​It was great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s ‌a big win for China too.
Here it is, the Apec family photo !
The gathering, hosted by China’s Xi Jinping , is attended by leaders from the 21-member grouping.
There has been ample speculation that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un may attend Apec , with Trump and US secretary of state saying they are willing to engage.
The Kremlin has also signalled Putin’s willingness to meet in Shenzhen.
In recent days the media has been tracking the elusive North Korean leader to assess his wheareabouts.
But there has been no sign of him in China so far , and photos released in recent days show him busy inspecting a tourism zone in Samjiyon .
And also a construction site in Hamgyong .
Kim’s visit to the construction sites in ‌the eastern province of the country could indicate the North Korean leader did not intend to attend Apec , said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at South Korea’s Kyungnam University, Reuters reports.
There is, it seems, plenty at home for him to do.
An update on the alleged global espionage scandal that unfolded in the lead-up to the Apec summit:
US President ⁠Donald Trump said he spoke to ⁠Chinese ⁠President Xi ​Jinping about artificial intelligence , but ⁠reference to former Nvidia CEO ⁠Jensen Huang only came ​up “briefly” ‌in ‌the discussion.
double quotation mark We did ‌not discuss it. I might have referred to it just briefly because ‌it’s such a tragedy. It’s ​a tragedy. He’s such a brilliant man,” Trump said ⁠in an interview ​to ​Fox News ​that was broadcast ​during ‌the network’s “The ​Ingraham ​Angle” show.
Jensen Huang ⁠resigned after revelations about extramarital affairs, including with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang , an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed and alleged Chinese spy.
The Guardian’s correspondent Rebecca Bailey is in Shenzhen, where she is covering the events of the day.
Describing the mood on the ground and what we can expect today, she writes:
There’s a sense of anticipation in the air, and traffic restrictions on the road, as we kick off the final day of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit. Today will be a blockbuster day of geopolitics , featuring both multilateral discussions and back-to-back big power negotiations .
Leaders from Apec’s 21 member states will shortly gather for a family photo, before going into a plenary session, according to a White House schedule.
Host Xi Jinping will then meet Donald Trump at a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park in the early afternoon. Just under two hours later Vladimir Putin will join them for unprecedented trilateral talks, according to that schedule. In addition, it has been reported that Trump and Putin might meet separately.
Also potentially on Thursday’s agenda is an Apec joint statement that, an official told Reuters on Tuesday, delegates had been “working around the clock” to find agreement on.

articles.title_orig: Iran War Updates: Gulf states and tankers under fire as U.S. and Iran ramp back up tit-for-tat strikes
articles.title_zh: Iran War Updates: Gulf states and tankers under fire as U.S. and Iran ramp back up tit-for-tat strikes
articles.content_orig:
In an interview with Fox News in China, President Trump said on Wednesday that there's indication that Iran is working on developing biological or chemical weapons because the U.S. has knocked out its nuclear capabilities.
Asked about a CNN report published this week on Iran's potential plan to detonate a so-called dirty bomb or a chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., Mr. Trump said people shouldn't be worried about the possible threat.
"Nuclear's much harder, and they're looking at gas and they're looking at the bio, you know, the biological weapons, not nice, and other things. And we'll see. We're going to have a new year coming up, and we'll see what happens after January 1," he said. "Look, if it does happen, we wipe them out."
Mr. Trump said the U.S. continues to talk to Iran, reiterating that Tehran wants to make a deal, but he wants one that will last. He also briefly reflected on the Memorandum of Understanding with Iran that was signed in June, calling it "a waste of time."
When asked if the memorandum was the reason for Vice President JD Vance being pulled off negotiations, the president said, "[Vance] is doing a very good job. No, well, he basically just left one thing out." He did not elaborate further.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform belonging to the Iranian-backed militant group on Wednesday.
Col. Turki Al-Malki, the spokesperson for the Coalition Forces, said on social media that the Houthis had used the platform in Saada, Yemen, in an attempted attack on Saudi Arabia's southern region.
The coalition's air defense was able to intercept and destroy a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis, Al-Malki said.
An unknown projectile struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations .
The maritime agency said local authorities reported that the incident took place north of Khasab, Oman. The projectile hit the engine room while the vessel was transiting outbound through the strait.
"The crew are safe and accounted for. Damage assessment, and environmental impact are unknown at the time of this report," the UKMTO said.
The USS George Washington has left the Middle East and is now in the 7th Fleet, the Navy's numbered fleet for the Indo-Pacific, a Navy official confirmed to CBS News on Wednesday.
That brings the number of aircraft carriers in the Middle East back down to two — the USS George H.W. Bush and the newly arrived USS Theodore Roosevelt .
The USS George Washington is homeported at Yokosuka, Japan, and may be headed back there along with the escort destroyers in the George Washington carrier strike group. The aircraft carrier, with its approximately 5,000 personnel, entered the Middle East in August to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln amid reports of low morale and food shortages aboard that carrier.
Yemen's Houthi militants on Wednesday targeted Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport and a financial center in Riyadh, Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said on social media .
Saree said "a large number of cruise missiles" achieved "precise and direct hits" on targets in Saudi Arabia's capital.
"This attack comes in response to the Saudi enemy's targeting of civilian infrastructure in our beloved country," he said.
The U.S. is warning Americans in Bahrain to be extra careful after at least four attempted strikes by Iran in the last week.
"Americans in Bahrain should exercise heightened vigilance due to the increased threat of armed attacks by Iranian-supported Houthis and Iranian efforts to target U.S. government officials and facilities in the region," the U.S. Embassy said in a new security alert issued Wednesday. "Be aware of potential alerts, flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions."
All of the launches were intercepted before causing any harm, according to U.S. Central Command. Iran was reportedly targeting U.S. radar sites in Bahrain. The latest round on Wednesday included attacks directed at Kuwait as well.
CENTCOM put out a statement on Wednesday afternoon saying no American military personnel have been injured in any of the strikes launched this week in a rebuttal to apparent rumors spreading online, it said.
The U.S. Treasury has targeted funding for the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group in its latest round of sanctions tied to Operation Economic Outcast.
One of the targets of the sanctions was the Wa Ta'awanu Association, which the U.S. said is a charity that "provides cover for Hizballah's activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services."
"The Iranian regime's attempts to infringe on Lebanon's sovereignty through terror proxies like Hizballah will not be tolerated," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. "The U.S. government will continue to disrupt Iran's attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies."
The sanctions also targeted an alleged gold and cash smuggling network run by Hezbollah and the IRGC's Quds Force.
The Hezbollah militant group has been fighting Israel in southern Lebanon for years, but the latest round of violence was sparked in the wake of the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in February. In solidarity, Hezbollah began targeting northern Israel with missile and drone launches, prompting an invasion by Israel.
The chief of Israel's military, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, met with U.S. Central Command leader Adm. Brad Cooper in Tel Aviv on Wednesday to discuss the current situation in the Middle East.
"During the meeting, the participants discussed regional developments and shared security challenges," Israeli officials said in a statement. "They also addressed the importance of deepening strategic and operational cooperation between the two militaries, strengthening coordination, and enhancing joint readiness to address a range of scenarios."
CENTCOM oversees military action in the Middle East and Cooper has become an important member of the Trump administration's Defense Department.
In addition, Zamir, Cooper and Mossad Director Roman Gofman took part in a trilateral meeting. Mossad is Israel's foreign intelligence agency, similar to the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency.
The U.S. and Israel have been debating whether to restart larger military action against Iran in the past several weeks after talks prior to Election Day fell apart. The U.S. launched a strike on Qeshm Island on Tuesday, which was categorized as self-defense after Iran had launched unsuccessful strikes against Bahrain multiple times this week.
A powerful explosion rattled homes in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents said, as Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis pressed their campaign of attacks against Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis also said they intercepted two cruise missiles — the latest in weeks of strikes targeting military, civilian and oil infrastructure.
Later on Wednesday, the coalition said it had intercepted two drones launched by the Houthis in the Riyadh and southern regions, after Saudi authorities had issued and later lifted an alert for the southern Sharurah governorate.
Residents said Wednesday's explosion came without warning, with no cellphone alert issued beforehand as is usually the case during aerial threats.
"The explosion was extremely loud," said a resident in northern Riyadh. "Hearing a blast without receiving a warning is very frightening."
An AFP journalist said doors throughout her home swung open and the lights briefly went out.
The location of the explosion was not immediately clear, but residents told AFP they saw smoke near Riyadh's airport in the northeast of the city.
U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said Wednesday that Iranian threats inside and outside the U.S. have "dramatically increased."
"We remain committed to detecting, deterring and combatting the Iranian lethal plotting outside the United States and inside the United States," Clayton told
